commands.statusTip: Stop the running recluster, drift or plugin job (its result is discarded), or a realignment of several clusters after the cluster in progress

commands.toolTip:
List the reserved chunk clusters (R0 … R99: the chunks a fiber-kit
chunk run left unsorted) in the cluster palette.  Unchecked, they
leave the palette and the displays, and Select All skips them.

Show the palette of the selected parent's child clusters (.clc).
Hidden, the selection, the displays and the matrices work on
the parent clusters.

Centre the curation matrices on the cluster selected in the parent or
the child cluster palette: the view pans so its diagonal cell is in the
middle (the zoom is kept).  A matrix panned completely off screen is
brought back to its upper-left corner either way.
Show the template-class palette (Templates mode).
Show the next feature space in the Space box (spaces that cannot be loaded are skipped).
Show the previous feature space in the Space box.
Toggle the selected cluster(s) as template units.  On save their linked template waveforms (.wtf) are written in every available method.
Run fiber-template now for the selected cluster(s) only, writing their linked template waveforms (.wti/.wtf).  Save first — the tool reads the clustering files on disk.

Renumber clusters so that similar clusters get adjacent IDs, using
single-linkage agglomerative clustering on the active similarity matrix.
When both error and template matrices exist, uses whichever was most
recently created or clicked.  Clusters 0 (artifact) and 1 (noise) are
preserved at the start.  Undoable with Ctrl+Z.

Renumber clusters so their IDs run from largest to smallest by spike
count (the biggest cluster becomes 2).  Clusters 0 (artifact) and 1
(noise) are preserved at the start.  Undoable with Ctrl+Z.

Renumber clusters so their IDs run by ascending starting time — the
cluster whose earliest spike comes first becomes 2.  Clusters 0
(artifact) and 1 (noise) are preserved at the start.  Undoable with Ctrl+Z.

Renumber clusters by descending refractory contamination — the
fraction of inter-spike intervals shorter than 2 ms.  The most
contaminated cluster becomes 2 (top of the palette).  Clusters 0
(artifact) and 1 (noise) are preserved at the start.  Undoable with Ctrl+Z.

Renumber clusters by descending mean-waveform SNR (peak-to-trough on
the best channel over baseline noise).  Best-SNR cluster becomes 2.
Requires computed mean waveforms — clusters without one sort last.
Clusters 0 (artifact) and 1 (noise) are preserved.  Undoable with Ctrl+Z.

Renumber clusters by descending peak-to-trough amplitude of the mean
waveform, taken on the channel where it is largest.  The biggest unit
becomes 2.  Requires computed mean waveforms — clusters without one
sort last.  Clusters 0 (artifact) and 1 (noise) are preserved.
Undoable with Ctrl+Z.

commands.text: Sort Clusters by Largest Amplitude by C&hannel
commands.toolTip:
Renumber clusters in blocks: one block per channel, in channel order,
each holding the clusters whose largest peak-to-trough amplitude falls
on that channel, ordered biggest first.  Requires computed mean
waveforms — clusters without one sort last.  Clusters 0 (artifact) and
1 (noise) are preserved.  Undoable with Ctrl+Z.

Renumber clusters by descending error-matrix merge affinity — each
cluster's highest same-neuron probability against any other cluster.
The strongest merge candidate becomes 2.  Requires a computed,
up-to-date error matrix in the active display.  Undoable with Ctrl+Z.

Renumber clusters using the residual matrix, gated by spike count.
Clusters with >= the prompted threshold go to the upper-left (low
ids), the rest to the lower-right; each block is seriated by
residual similarity.  Requires a computed residual matrix.
Clusters 0/1 are preserved at the start.  Undoable with Ctrl+Z.

Renumber clusters along a nearest-neighbour chain over their per-sample
MEDIAN waveforms (Euclidean distance): each cluster is placed next to
its most waveform-similar unused neighbour.  Reads the .spk file; needs
no matrix.  Preferences > Curation > Cluster order can use the mean
waveforms instead.  Clusters 0/1 preserved at the start.  Undoable with Ctrl+Z.

Renumber clusters by spectral (Fiedler) seriation of their per-sample
MEDIAN waveforms: orders clusters so the whole layout respects the
GLOBAL waveform structure, not just each cluster's nearest neighbour.
Reads the .spk file; needs no matrix.  Preferences > Curation > Cluster
order can use the mean waveforms instead.  Clusters 0/1 preserved at
the start.  Undoable with Ctrl+Z.

commands.statusTip: Split the selection into one new cluster per density basin in the active scatter view — selected atoms (one parent) in children view, selected parents otherwise.

commands.toolTip:
Test the selected cluster for hidden bimodality.  If a valley is
detected along one of its top-3 principal components AND the two-
cluster model beats the single-cluster BIC, split the cluster in two.
Partition the selected cluster into new sub-clusters using a K-nearest-neighbour vote against existing well-isolated clusters as references.

Cut the selected cluster into consecutive blocks of recording time.
Blocks start at the origin of the session, so the boundaries are the same for every cluster and the pieces line up in time.
Works on a parent or, in child view, on an atom.

With two similarly shaped clusters selected: every burst is given to the cluster of its first spike, and the later spikes of the burst that are in the other cluster are split off into a new cluster -- one per reference cell, only when the count stands above chance (unrelated firing, and cells firing together in no order).  With three selected: two references and a cluster that holds spikes of both; its spikes behind each reference's burst leaders are split off, one new cluster per reference.  With children selected it works on the child layer: the new clusters are new children beside the ones the spikes come from.  Undoable.

For each selected cluster: its spikes, centred on the first half crossing of their falling flank and seen through a tapered window around it on every channel, are put in the order in which each next one changes the cumulative mean waveform least.  The order is cut where a channel's cumulative kurtosis starts to rise, and the spikes past the cut are split off into a new cluster; the core stays.  It assumes one unit is more than half the cluster, and it errs on the side of splitting.  Reads the waveforms of the space shown.  With children selected the new cluster is a new child beside the one the spikes come from.  Undoable.
Split each selected cluster's waveform outliers (residual to its own median waveform) off into a new cluster.  Undoable.
Split each selected cluster's gain-free residual outliers -- on-channel (shape) and off-channel (position) terms, separately thresholded -- off into new clusters.  Undoable.

Designate one selected cluster as a waveform template and pull matching spikes out of the other selected clusters — normalized kernel-weighted median-waveform residual, restricted to the current channel selection.  Works in both scopes.
Pin cluster(s) as the fixed axes of the oblique (template-axis) view, so a different cluster can be projected onto them with Shift+O.

commands.statusTip: Recluster the selected cluster(s) with the active engine: KlustaKwik

commands.toolTip: Recluster the selected cluster(s) on the residuals of their pooled median waveform
Recluster using the highest-variance channels' features
One selected cluster is a mixture of the others: sort them pooled, and replace only the mixed cluster by its pieces (the references are left as they are)
Run the fiber-kit plan of this folder's fiber-kit.yaml on the selected clusters' spikes (a sub-session) and replace them with its clusters
Recluster runs KiloKlustaKwik on the selection's features (Preferences > Reclustering)
Recluster runs the fiber-kit plan on the selection's sub-session (the fiber-kit-recluster plugin's defaults, else the preferences' command)

commands.statusTip: Not installed: run `fk install klusters-plugin` (fiber-kit 0.66.3+), then Plugins > Reload Plugins
commands.toolTip: Recluster REFINES the selected unit(s): fiber-manifold fits the field manifold of their off-spike channels in sliding windows and installs the result as their children (the parents keep their ids; the manifold becomes a feature space under Space)
Re-align spikes in the selected cluster to their true peak, update .res/.spk/.fet files, and swap ordering if needed.

Run Realign Spikes on every cluster (skipping noise=0 and artifact=1) with its settings: the Refinement preferences and the Top-Channels spin box.  Each cluster's result is auto-accepted as a pending change; the batch can be stopped with Edit > Cancel Running Job (Ctrl+.).

Realign and nudge keep each spike in its own row, so the .res can drift out of time order.  This sorts the saved .res by time and moves the same rows in every method's .spk and .fet and in the .clu and .clc, then reopens the document.  Save first; undo history is cleared.

Bring every other feature space (method) of this group up to the current spike times: re-extract its waveforms from the .fil and re-project its features through its own PCA basis.  Use after realigning or nudging in the .clu's own space.  The results are working copies, written by Save.

commands.statusTip: Enable super-sampling in Preferences > Realignment first (high-end machines).
commands.toolTip: Build a waveform space with 2 spline-interpolated ticks per acquisition sample over the shown space (its own .spk, PCA basis and features), listed under Space.  Realign and nudge in it work at sub-sample resolution: the .res keeps whole samples, the rest is each spike's phase (the space's last feature column).  2× the waveform bytes and work: Preferences > Realignment > Super-sampling enables it.

commands.statusTip: Enable super-sampling in Preferences > Realignment first (high-end machines).
commands.toolTip: Build a waveform space with 4 spline-interpolated ticks per acquisition sample over the shown space (its own .spk, PCA basis and features), listed under Space.  Realign and nudge in it work at sub-sample resolution: the .res keeps whole samples, the rest is each spike's phase (the space's last feature column).  4× the waveform bytes and work: Preferences > Realignment > Super-sampling enables it.

commands.statusTip: Open a .clu saved under a super-sampled (_U) token first.
commands.toolTip:
From a super-sampled (_U) session: copy the saved .clu (and its .clc/.clp/.cli)
under the base-rate token, beside the base-rate .res/.spk/.fet -- the shared
.res and the synced base space -- without leaving this session.

Run ndm_estimatedrift on the current electrode group to estimate probe displacement over time.  Requires that this group is already curated (a .clu.N file exists).  Produces SESSION.drift alongside the data files.

Compute drift-adaptive chunk boundaries from SESSION.drift and optionally re-run KlustaKwik on the other electrode groups that share this probe.  Requires SESSION.drift (generate it first with 'Generate Probe Drift').

Make this flat clustering hierarchical: write a .clc child layer and a
.clp parent map next to the .clu, then reopen the session with the child
palette.  Every unit starts as one atom with the same id; split a unit's
atoms in the child palette from there.  An existing .clc that is nested in
the .clu is kept.  Unsaved edits are saved first; the undo history is cleared.

Break the selected parent(s) up: each child moves, whole and keeping its id,
to the parent whose template (mean waveform) it matches best among the
parents with more than a given number of spikes (default 100).  The children
matching none become parents of their own, the largest keeping the parent's
id, as Dissolve Parent does.  Shows the plan first.

Renumber both layers into the low integers with no gaps: parents become
2, 3, 4 … and atoms likewise, with the noise and artifact bins left in
place.  Occasional housekeeping after a long session of splitting.
The atom undo history is dropped, because it names ids that move.

Gather the selected parent's tiny children — the single-spike debris that
accumulates after repeated splitting — judged against the median waveform
of the parent's other children, the ones not being merged: those whose
shape matches are merged into one child, the rest stay as they are.
Nothing is deleted; the merged child is an ordinary atom of the same parent.

Gather the tiny parents (below a spike count) by the parent whose template
(mean waveform) each matches best among the parents that are not being
merged: those matching the same parent are merged into one new parent
beside it, and those matching none stay as they are.  The parents they are
compared with are not changed.  Works on the selected parents, or on all
of them when fewer than two are selected; shows the plan first.

Re-cut child atoms that now straddle more than one parent so each
atom belongs to a single parent again, and regenerate the .clp
parent map.  Run after reassigning / consolidating the parents.

Walk every parent and merge its child atoms into one self child
(numbered parent + 10000), so the atom layer becomes a copy of the
parent layer.  Discards all sub-mode structure -- undo with
Ctrl+Shift+Z.

Multi-lasso (Ctrl+5): closing a lasso keeps it instead of cutting.
Draw several, then Split by Lassos (Enter): each overlap pattern
becomes a cluster -- two overlapping lassos give three.
Split the kept multi-lassos by their overlaps (Enter)

Checked when the opened clustering has both a .clc child
and a .clp parent-map sibling — the session is then
hierarchical.  Determined by the files present at open, not
toggled at runtime; a flat .clu session is the alternative.

Add a residual-matrix display to the active view.  Cell (row A,
col B) is the variance of cluster A's spikes taken about cluster
B's mean waveform; the diagonal is A's within-cluster variance.
Press U to (re)compute it along with the error/template matrices.

Add a drift-matrix display to the active view.  Cell (row A,
col B) is the correlation between A's mean waveform shifted along
the probe depth axis by the slider's µm value and B's mean: +Δ
above the diagonal, −Δ below.  A unit pair split by probe drift
reads high at the Δ that realigns it.  Needs probe geometry
(the session YAML probes: section).

Open the template library for the open group: the marked units'
linked waveform series (.wtf/.wti).  Pick a unit and a link
(drift / adapt) and scrub its bins; select two or more units and
pin them as the oblique (template-axis) basis.  Mark units as
templates and save to build the library.
